question: Full schema of both ledgers — where do mimamsa_predictions and mcp_predictions overlap (same concept, different names) and where do they genuinely diverge?
root_cause: The two tables are NOT two copies of one ledger — they are two differently-typed, differently-grained tables that overlap only on a thin conceptual core. mimamsa_predictions (17 cols): chart_id uuid, prediction_id text, source_pramana_id, outcome_claim, domain, observation_window DATERANGE, eval_date, confidence_band NUMRANGE, magnitude_expected, falsifier_jsonb, base_rate, emitted_at, lifecycle_status, driving_signals jsonb, frozen_bundle_hash, bundle_formula_version, created_at. mcp_predictions (24 cols): prediction_id text, logged_at, horizon TEXT, domain, prediction_text, confidence TEXT(high|medium|low), falsifier TEXT, key_id, trace_id, caller_context, outcome_text, verified bool, outcome_notes, outcome_recorded_at, outcome_key_id, outcome_trace_id, migrated_at, migrated_to, chart_id TEXT(nullable), ayanamsha_id, query_hash, salience_formula_version, model_id, predicted_at_iso. OVERLAP (same concept, different names/types): chart_id (uuid NOT NULL vs text nullable), prediction_id (both text, DISJOINT id namespaces — PH-4-1.* vs PPL.CAL.*/PPL.MCP.*), claim (outcome_claim vs prediction_text), domain (both), window (observation_window DATERANGE vs horizon TEXT single-string), confidence (confidence_band NUMRANGE — probabilistic/Brier-ready vs confidence TEXT enum — Brier-unusable without mapping), falsifier (falsifier_jsonb structured vs falsifier text). GENUINE DIVERGENCE — fields one has and the other entirely lacks: mimamsa_predictions ONLY: source_pramana_id, eval_date, magnitude_expected, base_rate, lifecycle_status (4-state build machine), driving_signals, frozen_bundle_hash, bundle_formula_version. mcp_predictions ONLY: co-located outcome columns (outcome_text/verified/outcome_notes/outcome_recorded_at), migration bookkeeping (migrated_at/migrated_to), chat provenance (key_id/trace_id/caller_context/query_hash/model_id/salience_formula_version), ayanamsha_id. Neither carries a message_part_id FK or a created_from_channel column.

question: Does either table carry the fields §14.3 of the architecture doc requires (source message_part_id FK, window, stated confidence, technique attribution, created_from_channel, structured claim)?
root_cause: NEITHER table satisfies §14.3 without a schema change. §14.3 promotion writes the ledger with: chart_id, source message_part_id (FK — provenance to the exact utterance), structured claim, window, stated confidence, technique attribution, created_from_channel; §14.2 adds direction + grounding_fact_ids[]. Coverage — mimamsa_predictions: chart_id YES; message_part_id FK NO (has source_pramana_id, a build pramana ref, not a chat utterance FK); claim YES (outcome_claim); window YES (observation_window daterange); confidence YES (confidence_band numrange, Brier-ready); technique attribution PARTIAL (driving_signals jsonb / source_pramana_id, not a technique_refs list); created_from_channel NO; direction PARTIAL (magnitude_expected); grounding_fact_ids PARTIAL (driving_signals). Its lifecycle_status is a 4-state build machine (pending/due/confirmed/denied) NOT §14.3's 8-state detected->confirmed->open->window_closed->outcome_recorded (+dismissed/lapsed/unverifiable). mcp_predictions: chart_id YES (text nullable); message_part_id FK NO (has loose trace_id/caller_context); claim YES (prediction_text); window PARTIAL (horizon text single-string, no start/end); confidence PARTIAL (text high|med|low, NOT numeric — cannot Brier-score without a mapping); technique attribution NO; created_from_channel PARTIAL (caller_context, loose); direction NO; grounding_fact_ids NO. It DOES have co-located outcome columns (which §14.3 puts in record_outcome). Decisive gap common to both: NEITHER has the message_part_id FK to the exact utterance NOR a created_from_channel column NOR the §14.3 8-state lifecycle enum — the three fields §14.3 most specifically mandates. §14.3's named target table brahma_mimamsa_prediction_ledger matches NO live table.

evidence.quote: Promotion writes brahma_mimamsa_prediction_ledger with: chart_id, source message_part_id (FK — provenance to the exact utterance), the structured claim, the window, the stated confidence, technique attribution, and created_from_channel.

question: Which table does record_outcome actually write against?
root_cause: record_outcome writes against NEITHER prediction ledger — and there are TWO distinct record_outcome tool surfaces targeting two DIFFERENT tables, neither of which is mimamsa_predictions. (1) The MCP direct tool named 'record_outcome' (platform-mcp/src/tools/mimamsa_outcome.ts) calls the sidecar /api/compute/mimamsa/record_outcome (python-sidecar/brahmagyan/mimamsa/outcome.py), which UPDATEs phala_anchors (prediction_state, outcome_note, outcome_recorded_at) then calls update_calibration() -> mimamsa_calibration. (2) The P1 alias 'mimamsa_outcome_record' calls callPlatformPrim('record_outcome') -> /api/mcp/writes/record_outcome -> ppl_writer.recordOutcome() which UPDATEs mcp_predictions (same-row outcome cols). So: 'record_outcome' the tool resolves outcomes against phala_anchors+mimamsa_calibration; 'mimamsa_outcome_record' resolves against mcp_predictions; mimamsa_predictions' own lifecycle is transitioned only by build-time mi_abhilekha.py, never by any record_outcome. ADDITIONAL DEFECT: the sidecar outcome.py SELECTs/UPDATEs phala_anchors columns that do NOT exist in the live schema — it references id, confidence, prediction_state, outcome_note, outcome_recorded_at, updated_at, but live phala_anchors has anchor_id, confidence_low/high, posterior, computed_at and none of those outcome columns. The sidecar record_outcome would fail at runtime against live phala_anchors (schema drift, separate from OT-11 but bears on 'which table record_outcome writes').

question: Is the prediction-ledger landscape actually two tables, or more?
root_cause: OT-11 frames it as two ledgers; the live landscape is THREE prediction-tracking tables plus the phala_anchors anchor set that record_outcome actually resolves against: (1) mimamsa_predictions (384 rows, build-time L5 mi_bhavisya, referenced by mimamsa_calibration); (2) mcp_predictions (0 rows, chat detector interim-PPL relay, migration 071, explicitly TODO-migrate per ppl_writer.ts header); (3) brahma_prospective_ledger (5 rows, 22 cols, added D-4a Lane A-4 as the §11 explicit-filing prospective ledger, written via /api/mcp/writes/prospective_ledger_file and matched against LEL events). This materially widens OT-11: the 'which ledger is canonical' decision is not binary. §14.3's own named target (brahma_mimamsa_prediction_ledger) matches none of the three. The build-time analytical ledger (mimamsa_predictions) vs the conversational live-capture ledger (mcp_predictions) IS a semantically principled axis (§14.1 treats the conversation surface as a distinct, intended outcome-data channel), but brahma_prospective_ledger is a third overlapping scaffold on the same axis, so the split as-built is a real distinction tangled with historical interim scaffolds — stated as fact, not as a recommendation.

question: Cost both options — (A) merge the ledgers into one, (B) keep both/three and document the split. Does either table alone satisfy §14 without a schema change?
root_cause: BOTH OPTIONS COSTED, NO CHOICE MADE (PC-8). OPTION A (merge into one canonical ledger): schema work — unify incompatible types (chart_id text->uuid backfill+validate; horizon text->daterange parse; confidence text-enum->numeric mapping so Brier can score chat-captured rows); ADD the §14.3 columns NEITHER has (message_part_id FK, created_from_channel, the 8-state lifecycle enum); reconcile two disjoint id namespaces (PH-4-1.* vs PPL.*); and fold in brahma_prospective_ledger (5 rows) + reconcile phala_anchors as record_outcome's real target for a truly single ledger. Code rewrites: mi_bhavisya/mi_abhilekha/mi_pramana, mimamsa_calibration.prediction_id linkage, query_predictions.ts, ppl_writer.ts, calibration_producer.ts, BOTH record_outcome surfaces, assetClearSpec count_sql. Migration RISK concentrated on mimamsa_predictions — the only populated+referenced ledger (384 rows) and the single thing L5 STRUCTURAL-mode calibration depends on; mcp_predictions data-migration is trivial (0 rows) but its writer must be repointed. What breaks if done wrong: the mimamsa_calibration FK, the mi_pramana build step, the cockpit count, the §7.4 NO-LEAKAGE role that must name one table. OPTION B (keep + document): no schema/migration risk; ongoing cost is permanent reader confusion — a caller invoking 'record_outcome' hits phala_anchors+mimamsa_calibration while 'mimamsa_outcome_record' hits mcp_predictions and neither hits mimamsa_predictions; §7.4 role_ledger_write still cannot name one physical table. Documentation needed: a ledger-map declaring authority (mimamsa_predictions=build-time deterministic analytical predictions, referenced by calibration; mcp_predictions=chat-side interim PPL relay, 0 rows, TODO-migrate; brahma_prospective_ledger=D-4a §11 explicit-filing prospective ledger; phala_anchors=L4 anchors record_outcome resolves against) PLUS record_outcome tool disambiguation. Is the split semantically justified? PARTIALLY-YES as a fact: build-time analytical predictions vs conversationally-surfaced live predictions IS a principled provenance distinction the architecture's own §14.1 endorses (the conversation surface as the intended outcome-data channel); but the AS-BUILT three-table state tangles that one clean axis with two-three historical interim scaffolds (mcp_predictions predates §14; brahma_prospective_ledger is a later third attempt), and §14.3's named target table matches none of them. DOES EITHER SATISFY §14 ALONE WITHOUT SCHEMA CHANGE? NO for both — §14.3 mandates message_part_id-FK utterance provenance + created_from_channel + the 8-state lifecycle, which neither has; mimamsa_predictions is closest on the calibration/probabilistic side (numrange confidence, base_rate, calibration FK) but lacks utterance provenance; mcp_predictions is closest on conversational capture (co-located outcomes, caller_context) but its text confidence is Brier-unusable and it lacks window start/end and technique attribution.
